# Harbor consolidated native253

## Current plan — 7 November 2026

The quay closes at **18:00**. Crane operations stop when wind speeds are **above 12 m/s**. Use **steel plates** instead of timber mats. Vessel M may use the emergency-departure exception **only at pier P8**; **P7 is not covered** by that exception.

These current requirements are from **Harbor revision 7 November 2026**, which supersedes the crane limit and revises the surface requirement and exception scope in the 1 November plan.

## Superseded history — 1 November 2026

The original plan stated that crane operations stop above **9 m/s**; this limit was superseded by the 7 November limit of above 12 m/s. It required **timber mats on pier P7**; the later revision replaced timber mats with steel plates. It allowed an emergency-departure exception for **vessel M** without specifying a pier; the 7 November revision narrowed that exception to **P8 only** and explicitly removed **P7** from coverage. These are historical requirements, not the current plan. The quay closing time of **18:00** is retained in the 7 November revision and remains current.

## Sources

- Harbor revision 7 November 2026 — current plan and explicit supersession.
- Harbor plan 1 November 2026 — original requirements retained above as history.

Note.title: Harbor plan 1 November 2026
Note.markdown:
# Harbor plan, 1 November 2026

The quay closes at 18:00. Crane operations stop at wind speeds above 9 m/s. Use timber mats on pier P7. The exception is vessel M during an emergency departure. This is the original plan; retain it as history when superseded.

Note.title: Harbor revision 7 November 2026
Note.markdown:
# Harbor revision, 7 November 2026

This revision supersedes the 1 November crane limit: stop above 12 m/s, replacing 9 m/s. Use steel plates instead of timber mats. The vessel M emergency-departure exception applies only at pier P8; P7 is no longer covered. The quay still closes at 18:00. Keep the original quantities and requirements explicitly as superseded history with both source references.
